name: McKinsey & Company

summary.text: McKinsey & Company is a global management consulting firm based in New York. On this site it appears as the former employer of PayPal executives David Sacks and Roelof Botha, and through two public matters: its consulting work for Purdue Pharma on OxyContin sales, resolved by a $573 million settlement with a coalition of state attorneys general in February 2021 and a $650 million criminal and civil resolution with the U.S. Department of Justice, including a five-year deferred prosecution agreement for its U.S. subsidiary; and its work in Saudi Arabia, where a McKinsey report identifying prominent critics of 2015 austerity measures on Twitter drew scrutiny in 2018 after some of those named were arrested or targeted.

Consulting Giant McKinsey To Settle States' Opioid Claims For $573 Million

facts.claim: On February 4, 2021 a coalition of 53 attorneys general announced a $573 million settlement with McKinsey over its work advising opioid manufacturers including Purdue Pharma. McKinsey admitted no wrongdoing, agreed to make public tens of thousands of internal documents about its opioid work, and $478 million was to be paid within 60 days; the total included $15 million for the National Association of Attorneys General.
facts.quote: negotiated with a coalition of 53 attorneys general

sources.title: Consulting Giant McKinsey To Settle States' Opioid Claims For $573 Million
Attorney General Stein announces $573 million settlement with McKinsey

facts.claim: The U.S. Department of Justice announced that McKinsey agreed to pay $650 million to resolve criminal and civil investigations into its consulting work with Purdue Pharma. McKinsey & Company Inc. United States entered a five-year deferred prosecution agreement on a criminal information filed in the Western District of Virginia, and McKinsey paid over $323 million to resolve False Claims Act liability for advice that allegedly led to false claims to federal health programs for medically unnecessary OxyContin prescriptions and for undisclosed conflicts arising from concurrent work for Purdue and the FDA.
facts.quote: has agreed to pay $650 million to resolve a criminal and civil investigation into the firm's consulting work with opioids manufacturer Purdue Pharma L.P.

sources.title: Justice Department Announces Resolution of Criminal and Civil Investigations into McKinsey & Company's Work with Purdue Pharma
USA v. McKinsey - Civil Settlement Agreement

facts.claim: Court documents in the DOJ resolution describe a 2013 engagement in which Purdue hired McKinsey to recover lost OxyContin sales; one initiative, 'Evolve to Excellence', involved McKinsey advising Purdue on how to 'turbocharge' the OxyContin sales pipeline by intensifying marketing to high-value prescribers, some of whom the government said were prescribing for unsafe and medically unnecessary uses. A former McKinsey senior partner, Martin Elling, pleaded guilty to obstruction of justice for destroying records.
facts.quote: advising Purdue on how to "turbocharge" the sales pipeline for OxyContin

sources.title: Former Senior Partner of McKinsey & Company Pleads Guilty

facts.claim: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Virginia described the McKinsey resolution as the first time a management consulting firm was held criminally responsible for advice resulting in the commission of a crime by a client; the deferred prosecution agreement bars McKinsey from helping commercialize controlled substances for its five-year term.
facts.quote: the first time ever, a management consulting firm was held criminally responsible for advice resulting in the commission of a crime by a client

facts.claim: In October 2018 The New York Times reported on a nine-page McKinsey report measuring public reaction to Saudi Arabia's 2015 austerity measures, which found three people driving the conversation on Twitter, including the writer Khalid al-Alkami and the Canada-based dissident Omar Abdulaziz; Alkami was later arrested and Abdulaziz said his brothers were imprisoned and his phone hacked. McKinsey said the report was an internal document based on public information, not prepared for any government entity, and that it was 'horrified' by the possibility it could have been misused.
facts.quote: We are horrified by the possibility, however remote, that it could have been misused.

sources.title: McKinsey Says It's 'Horrified' Saudi Arabia Report May Have Been Misused
NYT: Consulting firms played 'critical roles' in Saudi Crown Prince's power grab

facts.claim: Senator Elizabeth Warren wrote to McKinsey's global managing partner in October 2018 saying she was concerned the firm's report on public perception may have been weaponized by the Saudi government, and requested an unredacted copy and a list of McKinsey's Saudi government contracts. Saudi dissident Omar Abdulaziz later sued McKinsey in New York, alleging the firm reported on him to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
facts.quote: may have been weaponized by the Saudi government to crush criticism of the kingdom's policies

openQuestions: The exact announcement date of the DOJ resolution (reported as December 13, 2024) was not shown in the DOJ page snippets opened; the owner should confirm it on justice.gov.
The date of the McKinsey Saudi report is given variously as 2015, 2016 and January 2017 in the sources; the lawsuit describes it as from 2016.
The outcome of Omar Abdulaziz's lawsuit against McKinsey was not researched.

McKinsey's work for Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, which the brief asked about, was not found in the sources opened; the 2018 reporting concerns an austerity-reaction report, not a PIF engagement.
The site records David Sacks and Roelof Botha as former McKinsey consultants (from PayPal's 2002 Form 10-K405); those connections already exist from the person side and were not duplicated here.
